Subject: MavenCloud RFI — draft responses for SCIM / SSO / admin controls

Team,

Attached is my first pass at the RFI responses from security/identity — file: Redwood_MavenCloud_IAM_Response_v1.pdf. Key sections I still want to firm up before sending to MavenCloud:

- SCIM: Marissa, can you confirm the incremental sync cadence (we currently support incremental polling with change tokens and push via SCIM 2.0 with batching up to 500 users per request) and whether we should call out delta token TTL? Also please add a short note about how we surface sync errors in the Console (per-user error lines, retry queue).
- RBAC / admin controls: Kimberly, please verify the role matrix and delegated-admin boundaries — specifically whether we should call the highest role "Org Admin" or "Tenant Admin" in the doc.
- SAML/OIDC: Neha, I've described both SAML 2.0 (IdP-initiated + SP-initiated, attribute mapping) and OIDC (groups claim + token refresh behavior). Can you add a brief note about session inactivity timeouts we recommend for enterprise customers and the optional step-up MFA hook we support?

I propose we send the finalized packet to Avery (MavenCloud Security) on Wednesday and offer a 60-minute identity deep-dive. If you could provide comments in the PDF by EOD Tuesday that'll be perfect.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: MavenCloud RFI — draft responses for SCIM / SSO / admin controls

Jordan —

Quick pass below (I'll also add inline comments in the PDF):

- SCIM cadence: Confirmed. We support SCIM 2.0 push provisioning and incremental polling. Delta token TTL is 24 hours by default; customers can opt for shorter TTLs via the Admin API.
- Error handling: Console shows per-resource error rows with a link to the provisioning log; we also emit webhook events for failed operations so downstream systems can alert.
- Bulk operations: We recommend batching users in groups of 100–250 for reliability; server-side accepts up to 500 but large batches increase processing time and can trigger retry behavior.

I'll attach a sample attribute map (scim_attribute_map_example.csv) and a short paragraph on conflict resolution (last-writer-wins by UTC timestamp, with an optional override via a provisioning webhook).

Marissa

Jordan —

Org admin naming: let's use "Org Admin (Tenant Administrator)" in the packet to reduce ambiguity.

Role matrix: confirmed. The roles we should list in the RFI are: Viewer, Operator (limited write), App Admin (can manage model routes & API keys), Org Admin (full tenant control). Note the separation between API key issuance (requires App Admin or Org Admin) and billing access (Org Admin only).

Audit trail coverage: we capture admin actions (role changes, API key creation, model pinning, rollout changes) with user, timestamp, IP, and action details. Logs are retained 90 days by default for hosted, longer retention available as an add-on or in Private deployments.

Kimberly

Subject: MavenCloud — Redwood IAM RFI submission and SCIM / SSO clarifications

Avery / MavenCloud team —

Thanks for sending over your RFI. Attached you'll find our completed responses and supplemental artifacts: Redwood_MavenCloud_IAM_Response_v1.pdf and scim_attribute_map_example.csv. Highlights below to make the review easier:

- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 (IdP & SP initiated), OIDC/OAuth2 (authorization code flow + PKCE for public clients). Group claims are supported via both SAML attributes (multi-valued) and OIDC groups claim; we can include group-to-role mapping in the Admin Console or manage mappings via SCIM.
- SCIM provisioning: SCIM 2.0 core + bulk extension. Push provisioning supported (outbound from IdP to Redwood) with incremental sync tokens and an optional polling mode for customers who prefer to pull. Delta tokens valid for 24 hours by default; we support filtering via "filter" param and group membership synchronization.
- RBAC & admin controls: Role model (Viewer / Operator / App Admin / Org Admin). Delegation: Org Admins can create scoped Admin roles with resource-limited permissions for specific teams; all admin activity is logged.
- Session & security controls: Configurable session idle timeouts (default 30m), optional step-up MFA hook, ability to enforce SSO-only auth for specific routes, and per-route token lifetime overrides for short-lived credentials.
- Evidence & audit: We can provide anonymized audit excerpts, SCIM sync logs, and Console screenshots for your reviewers. For compliance packs (SOC2/ISO), we have a standard evidence bundle available under NDA.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick sync to walk through the SCIM attribute map and group mapping patterns — do mornings this week work?
2) If helpful, we'll schedule a Cloud demo showing provisioned user lifecycle and admin audit traces.

Attached: Redwood_MavenCloud_IAM_Response_v1.pdf, scim_attribute_map_example.csv
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cRedwoodIAM/view

Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks for the packet and the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from our security team after an initial read:

1) Can you confirm how we should represent nested group membership in SCIM? Specifically, do you flatten nested groups or maintain group objects with membership pointers?
2) For attribute precedence, is it strictly last-writer-wins or do you have a per-attribute conflict policy?
3) Can you provide a customer reference who has used your SCIM push provisioning in production (preferably in the fintech space)?

We'd like to do the SCIM deep-dive on Friday at 10:00 AM PT if that works for your team. Also please upload the full evidence bundle to a shared drive (we'll share an access request) — we prefer the PDF + CSV + provisioning logs for the initial evaluation.

Appreciate it — Avery

Subject: Re: MavenCloud — Redwood IAM RFI submission and SCIM / SSO clarifications

Avery —

Thanks — Friday 10:00 AM PT works for Marissa and me. Answers inline below:

1) Nested groups: We represent groups as first-class SCIM group objects with membership pointers (so nested group relationships are preserved as group objects that point to members and other groups). For mapping into application roles we provide a flattening option in the Admin Console that evaluates transitive membership when you apply a group-to-role rule.

2) Attribute precedence: Default is last-writer-wins by resource timestamp (UTC). We can configure per-attribute precedence for select attributes (e.g., email) via provisioning policies if you need deterministic overrides.

3) Customer reference: We can introduce you to a compliance contact at LumaPay (fintech) who uses our SCIM push provisioning in production; I'll connect folks after the call.

I uploaded the full evidence bundle to the shared Drive link you sent and also attached the primary files to this thread: Redwood_MavenCloud_IAM_Response_v1.pdf, scim_attribute_map_example.csv.

Call invite: sent to the participants on this thread for Fri, Jul 2, 2027 10:00 AM PT — calendar link in invite.

Look forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Jordan
